disclaimer: Doses are general guidelines. Always follow the product label and your local agriculture officer / KVK.

paddy_rice_blast.name: Rice Blast
paddy_rice_blast.symptoms: Spindle/eye-shaped grey lesions with brown margins on leaves; neck rot in severe cases.
paddy_rice_blast.treatment: Spray tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6 g/L) or isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5 ml/L); repeat after 10-15 days if needed.
paddy_rice_blast.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, treat seed with carbendazim or Pseudomonas fluorescens.

paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Yellow to straw-coloured stripes from leaf tips and margins with wavy edges.
paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.treatment: Spray streptomycin sulphate + tetracycline (0.3 g/L) with copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L); drain the field briefly.
paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Balanced nitrogen, resistant varieties, avoid clipping seedlings, keep bunds and channels weed free.

paddy_brown_spot.name: Brown Spot
paddy_brown_spot.symptoms: Oval brown spots with grey centres on leaves and glumes.
paddy_brown_spot.treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L).
paddy_brown_spot.prevention: Correct potassium/silicon deficiency, use healthy seed, seed treatment with carbendazim.

paddy_sheath_blight.name: Sheath Blight
paddy_sheath_blight.symptoms: Oval greenish-grey lesions on sheath near water line that merge into large blotches.
paddy_sheath_blight.treatment: Spray hexaconazole 5 EC (2 ml/L) or validamycin 3 L (2 ml/L) directed at the lower canopy.
paddy_sheath_blight.prevention: Wider spacing, avoid excess nitrogen, remove weeds and stubble that carry sclerotia.

corn_common_rust.name: Common Rust
corn_common_rust.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
corn_common_rust.treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L) at first appearance.
corn_common_rust.prevention: Grow resistant hybrids, early sowing, remove volunteer maize plants.

corn_northern_leaf_blight.name: Northern Leaf Blight
corn_northern_leaf_blight.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves.
corn_northern_leaf_blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or azoxystrobin + difenoconazole as per label.
corn_northern_leaf_blight.prevention: Resistant hybrids, crop rotation, bury or remove infected residue.

corn_grey_leaf_spot.name: Grey Leaf Spot
corn_grey_leaf_spot.symptoms: Narrow rectangular grey-tan lesions bounded by leaf veins.
corn_grey_leaf_spot.treatment: Spray a strobilurin (azoxystrobin/pyraclostrobin) or triazole fungicide as per label.
corn_grey_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops, manage residue, improve air flow, resistant hybrids.

corn_maize_streak.name: Maize Streak Disease
corn_maize_streak.symptoms: Broken yellow-white streaks along leaf veins; stunted plants. Virus spread by leafhoppers.
corn_maize_streak.treatment: No cure for infected plants: uproot and destroy them; control leafhoppers with imidacloprid or thiamethoxam.
corn_maize_streak.prevention: Resistant varieties, timely uniform sowing, remove grassy weeds that host the leafhopper.

cotton_bacterial_blight.name: Bacterial Blight
cotton_bacterial_blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots turning brown/black; black arm on stems.
cotton_bacterial_blight.treatment: Spray copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L) + streptocycline (0.1 g/L).
cotton_bacterial_blight.prevention: Acid-delinted and treated seed, resistant varieties, destroy infected debris.

cotton_fusarium_wilt.name: Fusarium Wilt
cotton_fusarium_wilt.symptoms: Yellowing and wilting from lower leaves; brown streaks inside the stem.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.treatment: Soil drench with carbendazim (1 g/L) around affected plants; apply Trichoderma viride with farmyard manure.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.prevention: Resistant varieties, long crop rotation, balanced potash, avoid waterlogging.

cotton_verticillium_wilt.name: Verticillium Wilt
cotton_verticillium_wilt.symptoms: Yellow patches between veins turning brown (tiger-stripe); leaf drop, vascular browning.
cotton_verticillium_wilt.treatment: No effective chemical cure: remove badly affected plants; apply Trichoderma-enriched compost.
cotton_verticillium_wilt.prevention: Rotation with cereals, resistant varieties, avoid excess irrigation and nitrogen.

cotton_alternaria_leaf_spot.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
cotton_alternaria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small brown circular spots with concentric rings, often with a yellow halo.
cotton_alternaria_leaf_spot.treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L).
cotton_alternaria_leaf_spot.prevention: Balanced nutrition (especially potassium), remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation.

tomato_early_blight.name: Early Blight
tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target board) on older leaves.
tomato_early_blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or chlorothalonil (2 g/L); azoxystrobin for severe cases.
tomato_early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, remove lower infected leaves, mulch, stake plants.

tomato_late_blight.name: Late Blight
tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked dark lesions with white mould underneath in humid weather.
tomato_late_blight.treatment: Spray metalaxyl + mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or cymoxanil + mancozeb immediately; repeat at 7-10 day intervals.
tomato_late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, destroy infected plants, use healthy transplants.

tomato_leaf_curl.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus
tomato_leaf_curl.symptoms: Upward curling, crinkled and yellow leaves; stunted plants. Spread by whiteflies.
tomato_leaf_curl.treatment: No cure: uproot infected plants; control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps, neem oil or spiromesifen/diafenthiuron.
tomato_leaf_curl.prevention: Resistant hybrids, insect-proof nursery net, border crop of maize, remove weed hosts.

tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and grey centres on lower leaves.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Spray chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or mancozeb (2.5 g/L).
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Remove infected leaves, avoid wetting foliage, crop rotation.

chilli_leaf_curl.name: Chilli Leaf Curl
chilli_leaf_curl.symptoms: Leaves curl, pucker and become small; plants bushy and stunted. Spread by whiteflies/thrips/mites.
chilli_leaf_curl.treatment: Remove infected plants; control vectors with yellow/blue sticky traps, neem oil (3 ml/L) or recommended insecticide.
chilli_leaf_curl.prevention: Nursery under insect net, resistant varieties, remove weed hosts.

chilli_anthracnose.name: Anthracnose (Fruit Rot)
chilli_anthracnose.symptoms: Sunken dark circular spots on fruits with concentric rings; die-back of twigs.
chilli_anthracnose.treatment: Spray carbendazim (1 g/L) or azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) at flowering and fruit set.
chilli_anthracnose.prevention: Disease-free seed, remove infected fruits, avoid dense planting.

chilli_powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
chilli_powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on lower leaf surface; yellowing and leaf fall.
chilli_powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray wettable sulphur (3 g/L) or hexaconazole 5 EC (2 ml/L).
chilli_powdery_mildew.prevention: Good spacing and air flow, remove infected leaves.

chilli_damping_off.name: Damping-Off
chilli_damping_off.symptoms: Seedlings collapse at soil level; water-soaked stem base in nursery.
chilli_damping_off.treatment: Drench nursery with metalaxyl + mancozeb (2 g/L) or copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L).
chilli_damping_off.prevention: Raised well-drained beds, seed treatment with Trichoderma (4 g/kg) or thiram, avoid over-watering.

stem_borer.name: Stem Borer
stem_borer.symptoms: Dead heart in young plants, white ear heads at flowering; bore holes in stems.
stem_borer.treatment: Apply cartap hydrochloride 4 G (25 kg/ha) or spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.3 ml/L).
stem_borer.prevention: Pheromone traps, clip seedling tips before transplanting, destroy stubble.

brown_planthopper.name: Brown Planthopper
brown_planthopper.symptoms: Hoppers at plant base; circular patches of drying plants (hopper burn).
brown_planthopper.treatment: Spray pymetrozine 50 WG (0.6 g/L) or dinotefuran directed at plant base; drain water.
brown_planthopper.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen and pyrethroid sprays (cause resurgence), leave alleyways every 2 m.

leaf_folder.name: Leaf Folder
leaf_folder.symptoms: Leaves folded lengthwise with white scraped streaks inside.
leaf_folder.treatment: Spray chlorantraniliprole (0.3 ml/L) or flubendiamide (0.2 ml/L).
leaf_folder.prevention: Balanced nitrogen, remove grassy weeds, encourage natural enemies.

rice_hispa.name: Rice Hispa
rice_hispa.symptoms: White parallel streaks and blotches from adults scraping leaves; mines by grubs.
rice_hispa.treatment: Clip and destroy infested leaf tips; spray quinalphos 25 EC (2 ml/L) if damage is high.
rice_hispa.prevention: Avoid close spacing and excess nitrogen, remove grassy weeds.

thrips.name: Thrips
thrips.symptoms: Silvery scars, upward leaf curling, scarred fruits.
thrips.treatment: Spray spinosad 45 SC (0.3 ml/L) or fipronil 5 SC (2 ml/L); blue sticky traps.
thrips.prevention: Remove weeds, avoid water stress, neem seed kernel extract 5%.

aphids.name: Aphids
aphids.symptoms: Clusters of small soft insects on tender shoots; curled leaves, sticky honeydew.
aphids.treatment: Spray neem oil (3 ml/L) or imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 ml/L) / thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3 g/L).
aphids.prevention: Conserve ladybird beetles, avoid excess nitrogen, yellow sticky traps.

whitefly.name: Whitefly
whitefly.symptoms: Tiny white flies under leaves; yellowing, sooty mould; vector of leaf curl virus.
whitefly.treatment: Yellow sticky traps (10/acre); spray neem oil (3 ml/L), spiromesifen 22.9 SC (1 ml/L) or diafenthiuron 50 WP (1 g/L).
whitefly.prevention: Remove weed hosts, avoid repeated synthetic pyrethroids, border crops.

mites.name: Mites
mites.symptoms: Downward leaf curling, bronzing, fine webbing under leaves.
mites.treatment: Spray wettable sulphur (3 g/L), spiromesifen (1 ml/L) or fenazaquin (2 ml/L).
mites.prevention: Avoid water stress and dust, remove heavily infested leaves.

fall_armyworm.name: Fall Armyworm
fall_armyworm.symptoms: Ragged holes and sawdust-like frass in maize whorls; inverted Y on larva head.
fall_armyworm.treatment: Spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG (0.4 g/L) or spinetoram 11.7 SC (0.5 ml/L) into the whorl.
fall_armyworm.prevention: Pheromone traps, sand + lime in whorls, early uniform sowing, intercrop with pulses.

corn_earworm.name: Corn Earworm
corn_earworm.symptoms: Larvae feed on silk and kernels at the cob tip.
corn_earworm.treatment: Spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) or spinosad at silking; chlorantraniliprole if severe.
corn_earworm.prevention: Deep ploughing to expose pupae, pheromone traps, timely harvest.

fruit_borer.name: Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa)
fruit_borer.symptoms: Round bore holes in fruits with larva half inside.
fruit_borer.treatment: Spray HaNPV (250 LE/ha), emamectin benzoate (0.4 g/L) or chlorantraniliprole (0.3 ml/L); remove bored fruits.
fruit_borer.prevention: Pheromone traps, marigold trap crop, bird perches.

jassids.name: Jassids (Leafhoppers)
jassids.symptoms: Leaf edges yellow then reddish-brown and curl downward (hopper burn).
jassids.treatment: Spray imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 ml/L), thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3 g/L) or neem oil (3 ml/L).
jassids.prevention: Hairy/tolerant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, remove weeds.

pink_bollworm.name: Pink Bollworm
pink_bollworm.symptoms: Rosette flowers, bored green bolls, stained lint and damaged seeds.
pink_bollworm.treatment: Spray emamectin benzoate (0.4 g/L) or profenofos 50 EC (2 ml/L) when trap catch crosses threshold.
pink_bollworm.prevention: Pheromone traps / PB-rope, timely termination of crop, destroy crop residue and seed cotton stocks.

severity_advice.mild: Early stage. Remove affected leaves and monitor every 2-3 days; spray only if it spreads.
severity_advice.moderate: Spreading. Apply the recommended treatment now and re-check in a week.
severity_advice.severe: Severe damage. Treat immediately, remove badly affected plants and consult your agriculture officer.
